strategy.observation: Plausible’s core product is privacy-friendly web analytics that does not use cookies or collect personal data.
strategy.offer_link: That positioning gives paid search a clear hook: campaigns can target buyers actively searching for privacy-focused analytics or cookie-free alternatives, where the privacy claim is the main conversion lever.
hypotheses: They are willing to invest in acquisition channels beyond organic and word-of-mouth.
There is enough search demand around privacy-focused analytics terms to make paid search economical.
The co-founder is involved in growth decisions or would sponsor a paid acquisition test.
strategy.angle: Plausible’s cookie-free, no-personal-data positioning makes it a natural candidate for paid search aimed at people already looking for privacy-first analytics.
strategy.fit_reason: The offer matches the company’s category and differentiation closely: people searching for privacy-focused analytics are likely to have strong intent, so paid search could plausibly convert well for Plausible.

draft.subject: Privacy-first search
draft.body:
Plausible’s cookie-free, no-personal-data positioning makes paid search a clean fit.

People searching for privacy-first analytics or cookie-free alternatives already have intent. I run paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software products, mostly where the privacy claim is the main reason to click.

If you ever test that channel, should I send a few keyword themes and ad angles built around that intent?
